title: A Postcard for the Vow
premise: Odile Lockridge, a ghostwriter who has spent his career erasing himself from other people's stories, is hired anonymously to exchange letters with a stranger as research for a memoir he's secretly writing about his professional rival, publishing magnate Vivienne Ashcroft. The letters turn tender—until Odile discovers his pen-pal is Vivienne herself, each of them believing the other is someone else entirely. As duty to his contract demands betrayal and truth demands confession, Odile must choose between exposing her vulnerabilities for the memoir and protecting the love they've built on paper; in the end he burns the manuscript, confesses everything in one final postcard, and Vivienne—having already guessed and forgiven him first—meets him where the letters began.
about_author: Jonah Winterbourne is the pseudonym of a former publishing insider who spent a decade writing other people's truths before claiming one of his own. He lives by the sea, where he still answers every letter by hand.

chapters.title: The Muscle That Learns
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. A ghostwriter who treats love as a trainable muscle accepts an anonymous letter-exchange assignment meant to humanize the memoir he's ghosting about rival publisher Vivienne Ashcroft. His first letter is clinical, performative—but her reply disarms him with unexpected honesty. Emotional beat: guarded curiosity; the first crack in his belief that hearts can be contained.

chapters.title: Ink Under False Names
chapters.summary: Alternating POV between Odile and Vivienne, who writes under a pseudonym believing she's corresponding with a stranger arranged by her therapist. Their letters deepen into intimacy while, in person, their rivalry sharpens—she suspects a leak in her house and grows colder at work. Emotional beat: dramatic irony tightening; tenderness on paper, hostility in the flesh, and Odile's guilt beginning to fester.

chapters.title: The Handwriting on the Envelope
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. Sorting Vivienne's private papers for the memoir, he recognizes her handwriting—the pen-pal and the subject are the same woman, and his manuscript is a weapon aimed at her heart. His editor demands final pages within the week. Torn between loyalty to his contract and the truth of what he feels, he begins quietly gutting the exposé. Emotional beat: crisis of conscience; self-forgiveness begins with refusing to betray her.

chapters.title: A Postcard for the Vow
chapters.summary: Vivienne's POV reveals she identified his handwriting chapters ago and kept writing anyway, testing whether love could survive without masks. At the memoir deadline, Odile delivers burned ashes and a single postcard confessing everything. She meets him at the seaside mailbox where the letters began, contract voided, both finally unhidden. Emotional beat: catharsis and resolution—truth chosen over power, love over invisibility.
